steps.content: (Scene change)
Eastside's commercial strip blazes with neon into the night. Joan, planted in the most visible spot on the street, is now ringed by a swelling crowd.
The stream shows no signs of slowing down. Every refresh sends the viewer count soaring, and within minutes of going live, it's already wearing a "Trending" tag.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: "Oh they're not just similar, they're the exact same." "Fan goggles thick enough to stop bullets." ...Okay, okay. So there are actual humans in this chat. Good to know.
Joan settles into a groove, more self-assured by the second as she scrolls through the chat, her energy building with each message she reads out loud.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Tch. "Nobody singer trying to clout-chase"? Cute. I was playing bars before your idol was out of diapers.

[Live Chat] Scrolling rapidly: wait is this actually true?
ngl they do sound pretty similar
WHERE IS THE KITTY BRING BACK THE KITTY
pls play something else i've heard this song a million times
Just got here, someone catch me up?
Phanuel fan army incoming in 3 seconds
idk anything about music but yeah i hear it
She kinda slays actually
Where can I buy that guitar? jk
Jane monitors the backend from her own screen, saying nothing. But the surging attention—digital and real-world alike—sets something quietly on edge inside her.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Sales are the least of my problems now. Those'll be great. But if this stream keeps going, there goes my Bureau bonus... This is a tough call.
Ten thousand, then twenty thousand... the viewer count starts multiplying at an exponential rate.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Alright, unlike those clowns at Mirrormoon Entertainment, I actually respect intellectual property. So I'll just play a clip of Phanuel's trash song instead of the full thing.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Everyone still tuned in, listen real close. Then tell me it's not the same song I wrote years ago.
Joan dials up the volume. The same melody now plays twice over, layered through the stream in perfect unison.
[Performance]
The chat picks up speed. Phanuel lyrics and fan chants start flooding to the top... The ratio of Phanuel fans keeps climbing, their voices slowly drowning out everything else.

[Live Chat]
Phanuel is the original! A producer confirmed it! Stop spreading lies!
LMAO a couple chords match and suddenly it's plagiarism? Fake music experts everywhere
Phanuel works her butt off and you think you can just ride her fame??
Project files are so easy to fake, nobody's buying this
play both full versions so we can actually compare
Zero music knowledge but everyone's suddenly a producer in here
Jane is the first to sense something wrong. In one swift step, she positions herself in front of the camera, blocking both Joan and the billboard behind her from view.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Kitty would like to suggest: if the audio is causing any discomfort, please direct your attention to link number two.
${PlayerName}

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Noise-canceling earplugs used by Phanuel herself. Buy two, get one free. Qualifying orders receive a bonus fan sticker and fridge magnet.
A smile barely registers on Jane's face as she pushes through product pitches and pins listings, a one-woman dam against the swelling flood of coordinated comments from loyal fans.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Seriously? Get out of my shot.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Not in your shot. In your monetization funnel. Traffic is only worth something if you convert it.
Traffic, money... nothing but this filthy garbage. Joan smacks Jane aside and presses the evidence right up against the camera lens.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: For the people who actually care about facts, look. This is the project file from my old drive. Edit history right here, dates included. I wrote that arpeggiated sequence years ago. They took it, swapped out the patch, and shipped it as something new.

[Live Chat]
COPYRIGHT POLICE PULLING UP
Evidence logged. Phanuel's legal team is eating good tonight
WAIT I know her, she's from Anavrin right?
wonder how much the haters are getting paid tonight
Lol someone's bitter they'll never have Phanuel's success
you're just mad you can't make a banger so you start drama
The chat keeps rolling, denial and jeers flashing by one after another, the pauses between them shrinking fast.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Forget the fat cat, everyone, focus up. In your idol's new song, the key, the chord degrees, and that embellishment at the end of the chorus and how it rises and falls. It's exactly the same as mine. All of it. If that's not plagiarism, tell me what is.
The viewer count in the top right corner leaps to twenty thousand, then thirty.

It's already too late... The pink avatars with Phanuel-themed usernames were never the real enemy. Jane watches a surge of default-profile accounts with auto-generated numeric IDs flood the backend, and she knows: something far more coordinated is about to enter the fray.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Looks like clawing back to the top requires some invisible cat paws.
Jane strips off the clumsy paw gloves that have been holding her back, snatches up her terminal, and starts cycling through accounts at a breakneck pace, flooding the chat with counter-fire.
"Stop dragging Phanuel's name through the mud. The more you spam, the more neutral viewers side against her."
"Can someone who's listened to both give an honest take? Leave the fan goggles at the door."
"Are those talking points being handed out in your fan groups? Even the typos match. Show some originality at least."

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: What are you even saying? I'm here to show people the truth. You flooding the chat with this nonsense doesn't clear anything up.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: First, it's not nonsense. It's talking strategy. Second, I'm trying to show you the reality here. To these people, your expert analysis and complete fabrication sound exactly the same. They don't know the difference. They don't care.
Joan ignores Jane and turns back to her audience, but the crowd has already moved on. A video blasts from someone's phone, and laughter spreads through the onlookers like a wave.
She doesn't need to see the screen. That's her song, her voice, pitched up and chopped into a joke. A meme, already circulating.
She glances at Jane, still clumsily trying to shield the chat with that bulky cat costume. Joan seizes the phone right out of the livestream rig.
She has steeled herself for a straightforward fight—facts, evidence, debate. But the screen isn't showing arguments. It's showing her history, laid bare.

[Live Chat]
I know who she is, she fell out with her band
someone in Anavrin died, right? thought they disbanded years ago
I looked it up. Their lead singer was selling songs to big labels back then too
Internal money issues, now she's out here clout-chasing
West District trash, total joke
desperate for royalties she didn't earn
If her old music was so great, how come nobody's heard of it
Being nobody kept her safe. Now she's banking on drama for a comeback

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: ...So that's how you do things here... That's Eastside's idea of fair play.

At the heart of the bustling commercial strip, people crowd around her, phones raised, capturing every moment to turn into content and memes to share. Scattered laughter breaks out, bleeding into the Phanuel variety show ad blaring from the street displays nearby.
Only Jane remains bent over her phone, still trying to pin a few reasonable comments to the top of the chat and direct everyone toward the merch in the shopping cart.
Maybe she really doesn't understand how things work in Eastside. Joan looks at the stack of evidence that has traveled with her from one law firm to the next, and throws it into the air.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: You. "Phanuel's Little Sunshine." You're not sunshine. You're a doormat. She wipes her feet on you and throws you out, and you thank her for it. You believe whatever they feed you. Is your brain just whatever slop she poured in there? Can you even hear the difference between a song and noise?

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: And you, "Phanuel's Twinkling Star," don't think I wasn't talking about you too!

Sheets of white paper take flight on the urban wind, only to be trampled by indifferent pedestrians and flattened by passing cars. Joan's furious shouting grows louder, more desperate, and the crowd answers with a wave of mocking applause.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Haha... Fine! Fine, just perfect.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: You want garbage? Here's your garbage.
She reconnects her phone to the speaker, and the original instrumental of Phanuel's new song fills the livestream.
The next second, the screen cuts to black.

steps.speaker: Stall Owner
steps.content: Mmph mmph mmph!
This livestream contains content flagged for copyright infringement and is now under review.
(Scene change)
That’s valuable information—hard to come by. Maybe we should consider an intel exchange.

Eastside's online discourse has already moved on to the next thing. Joan's brief attempt to defend her rights played out like a farce, forgotten the moment it ended. Only a handful of people are still watching the meme edits and clipped recordings of the whole spectacle.
Joan slowly slides her guitar back into its case, turns around, and holds out both hands to Jane.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: ...You're not going to run?

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: The Bureau knows I'm out. What's the point? My own music gets zero protection. I sing two lines of a stolen song, and I'm the one who gets silenced. So tell me. Whose rights does "copyright" actually protect?

A handful of young people fresh from a party wander past, drunk and rowdy, humming Phanuel's latest hit as they jostle each other. Passing by, one of them bumps into Joan's shoulder—on purpose or not, it's hard to tell. For once, Joan doesn't snap at them.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Don't give up yet. We almost made it work. We can try again. Keep playing, and keep singing, until everyone has no choice but to listen. You're bound to be remembered that way. Once the account gains traction, getting your rights back will be a lot more doable. And I could always use the extra cash.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Yeah, no thanks. That's exactly what I can't stand about you Eastside types. Always telling people how to live.
[Scene Change] Bureau Interrogation Room

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Unauthorized departure from supervision. Forged exit documents. Public disturbance. Joan, do you understand what these charges mean?

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: Yeah. I know. Can you just get through it? I'm exhausted.
Beside her, Jane files the assistance report, then adds a separate statement documenting the livestream account ban and her lost commission earnings.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: What are the odds I can recover any of this?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...I'll see what I can do.

Nightingale scans the densely written statement, a full page of explanation, and lets out an uncharacteristic sigh. Her gaze shifts to Joan, standing off to the side with her arms folded and her face turned pointedly away.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Jane. Based on tonight's event, do you assess Joan as being at risk of losing control?

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: She's not at risk. One, she couldn't beat me if she tried. Two... I think she just snapped for a second. I've been there.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: ...Nobody asked you to defend me.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Take her to confinement for now. We wait until Chief returns to determine formal disciplinary action.
